articles.title: FITBIT EDGE: PREMIUM DESIGN FOR AN ACTIVE LIFE
articles.summary: Fitbit Edge pairs the brand's largest, brightest Hybrid OLED tracker display with a tactile side button for quick control mid-workout, even with sweaty fingers. A subtly curved chassis of 100% recycled aluminum keeps sensors against the wrist for 24/7 heart-rate and sleep tracking. Four finishes, four redesigned band styles, and up to seven days of battery life round out the design.

articles.title: OPENAI NOW LETS YOU TEXT YOUR CHATGPT DOT AGENT TO GET THINGS DONE
articles.summary: ChatGPT Dot can now communicate through iMessage and RCS, letting users assign tasks, send photos or voice notes, and receive proactive updates without opening ChatGPT. Dot can use context from ChatGPT conversations and connected channels to decide where updates belong, while users can specify that only urgent information should arrive by text and approvals still happen inside ChatGPT. The beta is currently limited to ChatGPT Pro users in the US, with one-to-one messaging supported but no group chats, regular phone calls, or FaceTime.

articles.title: WINDOWS SECURITY IS FINALLY GETTING THE WINDOWS 11 MAKEOVER IT SHOULD'VE HAD YEARS AGO
articles.summary: Microsoft is redesigning Windows Security to finally align its interface with the rest of Windows 11, replacing layouts and visual elements that still feel inherited from an older generation of Windows. Navigation, typography, spacing, colors, controls, dialogs, and status indicators are being modernized, with layouts also adapting more consistently across different window sizes. The update additionally improves how security status and available actions are communicated, while device information on supported managed PCs will progressively load so useful details appear sooner.

articles.title: NOBODY ASKED FOR THE SPARKLE BUTTON
articles.summary: Products, from note apps to banks, ship the same AI chat panel behind a sparkle icon, often switched on by default and hard to turn off. Big cloud firms are projected to spend more than their cloud revenue on capex, while a cited study found that 95 percent of companies saw no measurable return from generative AI pilots. The fix is to build features with AI, not AI features, and to ask who asked, what it's named after, and whether it survives off by default.

articles.title: THE SYSTEM I NO LONGER KNOW BY HEART
articles.summary: Working with AI agents means the author no longer memorizes every detail of the design system they build, a shift that requires making systems legible to LLMs. That knowledge has to move into the system itself, through explicit naming, current documentation, and composition rules, since agents can't rely on informal context or unwritten history. Understanding why the system works still matters, but less inventory in the designer's head is a trade worth taking if the system knows more about itself.

articles.title: BUILDING AN AI-READY DESIGN SYSTEM LIBRARY: CODE → FIGMA WITH MCP. HANDS-ON GUIDE
articles.summary: Figma captures only part of the behavior encoded in production components, leaving AI to invent missing details such as focus order, error states, accessibility behavior, and failure handling when translating designs directly into code. Reversing the workflow makes code the source of truth and Figma its visual mirror, with AI and MCP transferring real tokens, styles, properties, variants, and states from a repository into a usable design library. Storybook provides designers with a visual view of the production system, while explicit documentation of anything that cannot be represented in Figma helps maintain parity instead of allowing invisible differences to accumulate.

articles.title: NO-CODE AI APP BUILDER
articles.summary: Create a website, internal software, customer software, or a mobile app with AI. Describe your business, preview and edit with AI, then publish with a paid plan.

articles.title: CREATE & EDIT AI VISUALS
articles.summary: Generate images, decks, carousels, and posters with AI — then edit every layer and export a finished, ready-to-publish result.

articles.title: ACCESSIBILITY CHECKER & WCAG 2.2 AUDIT TOOL
articles.summary: One in six people experience the web differently than you think. pour shows you what's getting in the way, and exactly how to fix it.

articles.title: YOU ARE THE BEST ARTIST
articles.summary: Art is less about conveying emotion to an audience than about capturing it, since a painter alone in a studio still makes art. Comparing skills with others can help, but becoming a better artist is personal, because nobody can express someone's feelings like they can.

articles.title: DESIGNING A SKILL
articles.summary: Agent skills can be treated like apps whose interfaces happen to be written largely through instructions, with both the human invoking the skill and the AI interpreting it acting as users. Building a polished skill requires many familiar design practices, including finding the right form, refining copy, creating a visual system, anticipating repeated use, offering meaningful customization, and testing across different contexts. Precise instructions matter because agents fall back on familiar patterns when given vague directions, making skills a useful place to encode the context, trade-offs, intuition, and taste that individual prompts cannot reliably communicate.

articles.title: THIS 3D ARTIST ACHIEVES INCREDIBLE REALISM TO BREATHE LIFE INTO STRIKING CHARACTER DESIGNS
articles.summary: A smug goblin, an albino demon, an adolescent chimp, and a dark elf showcase the striking realism of Australian 3D artist Tom Newbury.

articles.title: BIOLUMINESCENT ALIEN WORLDS THAT WILL MAKE YOU WANT TO PACK YOUR BAGS FOR THE COSMOS
articles.summary: Vancouver-based 3D artist Calder Moore builds bioluminescent forests, glowing flora, towering monoliths, and surreal planetary systems under twilight or starry skies.
